rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent oblique mass in each view, but the section is weakly programmatic for neighborhood living. It sits on the parcel and does not obviously collide, yet the dominant gesture is still close to a generic folded/leaning hall object rather than a street-building with an active ground threshold. The blue frontage edge is answered only indirectly; there is no convincing public void, court, undercut, or entry seam opening toward the access side. The silhouette has some continuity, but the stepped/tilted roof reads more like an abstract sectional gesture than a capacity-aware neighborhood mass. Overall it is repairable, but not yet program-fit.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a clear central void and an upper connector can support neighborhood-scale publicness.
